note: Expected outcomes are written from the frozen task contract, not recorded from a run. Ownership is an exact literal pathset of regular files: a declared path owns itself and nothing else, and a path that exists today as anything but a regular file is refused. Task state is machine-local, so a task operation changes nothing inside the repository at all - the zero-tolerance quantities below include the Git directory. Owned paths are compared as escaped display text, which is unambiguous and reviewable; the raw byte round-trip is asserted separately by the arbitrary-byte case.
platform_restricted_cases: A case may declare a platform restriction. It is reported as skipped with its restriction named on machines it does not apply to, and never dropped from the listing.

cases.description: One regular file declared, shown, and ended. The shape every other case is a deviation from.
An untracked regular file. Tracked or not makes no difference to a declaration.
A path that does not exist yet - the normal case when the task is about to create it. A declaration is not an observation.
A declared path that exists today as a directory. v1 owns an exact pathset of regular files, so a directory declaration has no meaning in it.
A symlink to a file and a symlink to a directory. Both refused as links rather than judged by their targets: v1's owned-path and content semantics are defined over regular files.
A FIFO. Not a regular file, so not something a v1 task can own.
Two spellings of one path in one declaration. Refused rather than merged: silently agreeing with half of what the user typed is not an answer.
'docs' and 'docs/guide.md' are two distinct declarations. Under exact ownership neither implies the other.
A trailing separator is not part of a path's identity, so 'docs//' is the path 'docs'.
Every declared name here is a filename, not a pattern: glob characters, pathspec magic, and arguments that look like flags. Nothing expands.
Names containing a space, a tab and a newline. Stored literally, rendered escaped, and the newline does not become a second output row.
'--own ../src/strategy.py' typed from tests/ means the same path as declaring it from the root, and produces the same digest.
Absolute paths, parent escapes, the repository root, the Git administrative directory, and '..' after a named component. All refused, and none leaves a task behind.
A repository with no commits. A task records the commit it started from, so starting one is refused - while doctor and status still answer, and nothing is written.
doctor, status and a refused start create no machine-local salt. The first successful start creates it: 32 bytes, readable by its owner alone.
Three staged entries the task never mentioned. The count is recorded informationally, the index is byte-identical across the lifecycle, and no filename reaches the output.
A repository with staged work it did not ask AIQE about. The index is byte-identical across start, status and end.
A repository pointing at commands every way it can - clean filter, fsmonitor, shell aliases, an executable hook. Declaring a task runs none of them.

Two linked worktrees share a common Git directory and have different per-worktree ones, so they derive different machine-local keys and hold two independent tasks. Neither writes inside any Git directory.
Two real processes racing to start a task in one worktree. One wins, one is refused, and exactly one valid record exists.
A process killed mid-write leaves a temporary file that was never renamed. It is not a task: status says so, and the next start succeeds.
An active record that cannot be read is unknown, not unsupported: status and start exit 2. 'task end' discards it, and that is the documented way out.

An active record written under a superseded schema. Reading it under today's semantics would say something untrue about a live task, so it is refused and left untouched. 'task end' discards it; there is no migration.
A symlink planted where this worktree's machine-local state belongs. AIQE refuses rather than writing through it to somewhere it never promised to write.
An owned path whose bytes are not valid UTF-8, declared through the real entry point with byte-preserving argv. The stored bytes equal the bytes typed.
